_comment: Local executor configuration. DATA, not code — swapping models must not require a code edit.
Measured on this machine 2026-09-10 (AMD RX 7800 XT 16 GB, Ryzen 7 5700X, DDR4-2400).
Rule of thumb that produced this choice: pick a model that fits ENTIRELY in VRAM.
Prompt throughput decides agent usefulness, not generation throughput — an agent spends
its budget reading. A 30B MoE spilling 6.3 GB to DDR4-2400 measured 8 tok/s prompt,
which is ~50 minutes to read a 25k-token file. See tools/local_executor/README.md.

measured.gpu: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT 16 GB (ROCm, gfx1101, native Windows — no WSL2)
measured.note: think:true measured 3971 tokens/92s for output identical to 136 tokens/3.0s at think:false

rejected.reason: 18 GB against 15.8 GB VRAM; 6.3 GB spilled to DDR4-2400
rejected.note: Figures corrected 2026-09-11 by npm run local:benchmark; the superseded prompt figure (8 tok/s) could not be reproduced. Still rejected: 6x slower to read than qwen3.5:9b.

rejected.reason: dense ~16-17 GB exceeds VRAM; a dense spill is worse than an MoE spill because every parameter is active per token
needs >45 GB for 4-bit; 44 GB combined ceiling. 2-bit would fit but degrades a code model where it matters most
18.6 GB against a 16 GB card; spills to DDR4. Slowest generation measured on this rig.
rejected.note: Present on this machine but not pulled by the harness. Benchmarked 2026-09-11 for completeness; it loses to qwen3.5:9b on both axes.

keep_alive_note: Measured 2026-09-11: a warm model loads in 3ms, a cold one timed out a dispatch and reported itself as "ollama not running". Residency is cheaper than the misdiagnosis.
max_parallel_note: Measured 2026-09-11 on this 16 GB card with a 9B model: two concurrent requests overlapped 12.9s of 27.7s serial work. Slots share VRAM; raise only with a new measurement. (An earlier draft of this note said 12GB — wrong, and corrected: the measured GPU is the 16 GB RX 7800 XT recorded in `measured.gpu`.)

benchmark_2026_09_11.conclusion: qwen3.5:9b holds: 6x the prompt throughput and 4x the generation of either 18.6 GB model, both of which exceed this 16 GB card and spill to DDR4. A code-specialised model does NOT win here — the size penalty dominates the specialisation.
benchmark_2026_09_11.discrepancy: The `rejected` entry below recorded qwen3-coder at 8 prompt tok/s. Re-measured at the SAME 32768 context it is 253.5 — a 31x gap that num_ctx does not explain, so the original figure is unsound (most likely taken during a cold load, or with another model still resident). The REJECTION is unaffected: 253 against 1508 is still a 6x loss. The number is corrected rather than quietly kept, because a wrong figure in an evidence file is worse than no figure.
